history.content: What is crop association exactly?

draws.answer: It is a group of two or more crops grown at the same time on the same plot, and the catalogue counts associations among its methods. In the south, Maritime and Plateaux, maize is usually grown with other crops, which it calls intercropping. In Centrale, Kara and Savanes it is more commonly grown together as a band of maize, cowpea, groundnut or cassava, with millet, sorghum, yam or okra following. The rule to follow when associating is that the two or more crops should not compete for the same nutrients, for light or for the space. Turn the leaves over and count the insects on several plants before deciding to treat. If whiteflies are dominant, place yellow sticky traps to catch the adults. Remove and destroy the most infested leaves and keep the plot edges free of weeds that host the pests. For a heavy attack, ask ICAT for the approved product and its rate. Make sure to harvest the groundnut at the right time so that the crop does not drop its pods early. For information on resistant varieties and fungicide use, contact ICAT.

per_item.reference: Now that your maize is at panicle initiation, you should top-dress with urea. For a half-hectare field, use 50 kg of urea, which is the 100 kg per hectare rate applied to 0.5 ha. If you want a soil-specific adjustment, go to ICAT for guidance.

history.content: I have a half-hectare maize field. I put the base NPK bags a couple of weeks after sowing, and now the plants are just starting to form tassels. What should I do next?

draws.answer: At this point you should apply the top-dress urea, 100 kg per hectare, which is the same as the base NPK 15-15-15 dose you put 30 days after sowing. Then weed the field at 15-25 days after sowing. When the maize reaches panicle initiation about 30-35 days after sowing, apply the top-dress urea. Avoid a split nitrogen application on a curve; wait for the uniform colour. To match the specific variety to your local conditions, visit ICAT.

You should now split the NPK 15-15-15 equal to 55 kg per hectare, which is 17 kg for your 0.5 ha field. Apply the top-dress urea at 100 kg per hectare, which equals 50 kg. Before you do the split, have the base NPK ready so you can mix the last dose. Plant the maize on ridges after a heavy rain, placing 3-5 grains per pocket at 3-5 cm depth using 7-10 kg of treated seed per hectare. The exact pocket spacing is 3 cm for varieties under 90 days, 5 cm for 90-100 days, or 7 cm for longer cycles. Do not grow maize until the soil is secure, after the first weeding and earthing-up. For a variety suitement and exact urea rate, see ICAT.

per_item.reference: Tiny critters under the leaf underside and yellowing tomato leaves are a sign of whiteflies or aphids feeding on your crop. First shake each tomato plant and inspect the underside to know which pest you are dealing with, because each needs a different method. Remove and destroy the most heavily infested leaves and keep the surrounding weeds cleared. For whiteflies, hang yellow sticky traps to capture the adults. For aphids, apply a strong jet of water and encourage ladybirds and lacewings. If the pest pressure is high, seek ICAT for the approved product and its rate. history.content: If I only have half that money, can I start at half the size?

draws.answer: Yes, and the brochure's own advice is to take the largest unit of the seven and scale it: a group of 30 hens and 3 cocks is the unit that needs an impounded water point, a breeder compartment, and a chick room, while a family of six needs at least six. So your half will have two of the groups and three of the compartments, and it will be a group anyway, because the plan is designed so that it exists as such. The same rule applies to the equipment: the gas incubator of 300 eggs suits a flock of 60 breeding hens, so a flock of 30 hens needs one of three rather than one. Remove and destroy any strongly mottled or stunted plants to stop spreading the virus. For clean cuttings you may consult ITRA or a registered producer, and ICAT can confirm the disease.

history.content: My corn in Savanes is getting older leaves that look pale yellow while the new ones stay dark green, and the stalks are thin. What do I do?

draws.answer: The pale yellow on the older leaves is a sign of nitrogen shortage on a soil that has lost organic matter. First, recognize that the uniform pale yellowing is hunger for nitrogen, not a disease, so fungicide will not correct it. Do not buy a broad-spectrum NPK mix or a systemic fungicide on a merchant's word, because mineral fertilizer alone often does not pay back on depleted soils. Bring back organic matter by adding manure, compost, or by leaving or burying the maize residues instead of burning them. Keep the second weeding and earthing-up on their normal schedule. For a soil analysis and the proper dose, go to ICAT.

The pale yellow leaves and thin stalks are signs of nitrogen shortage caused by soil depletion. draws.answer: Drain the water from the manure pit so the water runs rather than standing, and you should build the pit at least 1.5 m wide, 2 m long and 1 m deep with an apatam over it. The pit works on two principles: turning the droppings into something the fields can use, and limiting the spread of disease. This method is one of the seven waste management practices in the technico-economic reference.

You should drain the water from the manure pit completely and rebuild it so it is a doublet with a manure layer and a site. Build the pit at least 1.5 m wide, 2 m long and 1 m deep, covering about 90 m2 for the whole area. After the pit is dry, spread a 5 cm layered litter on the inside, then add the droppings, and keep the building as a footbath at the entrance. This method stops the spread of disease through droppings and urine. For a safe, disease-controlled pit, see ICAT.

Plant a resistant improved 55-75 day variety when the rains are strong, usually from mid-June to early July. Perform the first weeding about two weeks after sowing. Spray three times around flowering: first spray at 30-35 days when buds appear, second spray ten days later, and third spray ten days after the second, using an approved product at the label rate. The catalogue gives you five options for the arrangement: regular spacing, where the pegs go every 100 cm, and 80 cm apart; irregular spacing, with fewer pegs and gaps larger, 60 cm by 60 cm; lowland, with pegs at the water level lines; and bunds built with trees, with pegs at the base of the main bund and along its lowland side. The reason is that the catalogue puts pegs to mark the plan out on the site before a single hole is dug, so they are there before you start digging, and they are a way of following it rather than a way of cutting it.
